title: checklist test-fix: access-security.security-catalog-one-holder-and-boot-report acceptance[1] expects conflicts[] on the install-local refusal, which that door's ledger contract does not carry
body:
QA-source: #24558 · access-security.security-catalog-one-holder-and-boot-report · acceptance[1]

Disposition of a `fail` from the 18.0 release QA sweep (subject `5b14b7f3`) under the checklist-test SKILL §5 four-way table: **assertion defect** — confirmed by an independent RUNNER rule 7 re-derivation.

## The red row

Clause: "install-local of a package redeclaring a catalog name → 422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT (or PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED) with conflicts[], and nothing is recorded as installed". Live (scratch copy of the showcase, two different packages): 422 `{code:"PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED", message:"…"}` — keys `code` and `message` only; the conflicting names and their holders are named inside the message. Nothing was installed (package count 27 → 27, install-local list empty), so the second half holds. Reproduction: #24558 "Fails" section.

## Why the clause, not the product

- The thrown `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError` does carry `.conflicts` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`), but the install-local door (`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` ~1593–1602) answers its OWN registered `PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` at 422 interpolating only the message — the documented contract of that route in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (~999–1003).
- No pin in the item's `automated.ref` asserts `conflicts[]` at this door; the one-holder pin asserts `.conflicts` on the boot-refusal throw.

## Proposed edit (for the item's owning seat; this wave makes no checklist edit)

Re-point acceptance[1] to "422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED whose message names each conflicting name and its holder, and nothing is recorded as installed" (holds today). A structured `conflicts[]` on this door would be a product enhancement, a separate decision.
